evidence.detail: Direct inert-report handler probe records acceptance/buffer mutation for wrong and unknown sessions; it explicitly does not establish a complete aggregation exploit.
Existing Phase 2 security acceptance already covers session-to-client identity, wrong/unknown/stale-session rejection, bounded payload checks and trusted-peer pickle limits.
Report handler deserializes and creates session buffers without verifying sid/client assignment.
Physical worker sessions are reassigned to server-selected logical client IDs.
Urgent async reports may use a different client ID; current server-issued assignment/request context, including edge behavior, must determine valid identity.

assessments.conclusion: The probe strengthens already-planned 2B acceptance with 2D payload coordination, not a new feature or authentication scope. Identity validation must precede unsafe parsing/unrelated mutation while preserving legitimate worker reuse and urgent/edge reports. Session binding is not cryptographic authentication and does not make pickle safe for untrusted peers.
